name: Article body
summary: Long-form article body text (paragraphs, headings with anchors, lists, quotes and pull quotes, pictures, galleries and picture sizes, callouts, tables, inline marks, click-to-load videos and chart figures) styled by one class layer, lib/article.css, under a single .aha-article-prose root. The same file styles the public library article page and the article editor canvas, so what an editor writes is what a reader sees.
highlights: The same body on the library article page and the editor canvas
Videos load the player only when the reader clicks play
Chart figures keep their numbers in a Show data table
lead: Load lib/tokens.css and lib/article.css, then wrap the article HTML in one element with the class aha-article-prose. Plain elements need no classes; only the callout, the table wrapper, the pull quote, the gallery, the picture sizes, the video and the chart figure carry one. Cards and the FAQ come from DS components and sections (Compose with, below).

skillRef.note: Authored in the DS. The class layer is lib/article-css.js, written to lib/article.css by generate.mjs; screen-lint checks the classes a page uses against it.

composedOf.use: the callout tone glyph: <aha-icon name="system-info|system-lightbulb-filament|system-warning-circle" size="24"> in the default icon ink; system-play (32 px) in the video play circle; system-caret-down (16 px) on the chart Show data summary
the one action in a promo callout
the chart in a chart figure: <aha-chart palette="brand"> (column, bar, line or donut) inside figure.aha-article-chart
the Course or Game label on a card, color="category"
lays out a row of cards, min="220"
link colour at rest and visited; hover is --aha-text-link-hover

rules.rule: Put the whole article body inside one .aha-article-prose root and load lib/tokens.css then lib/article.css. Never restyle the body elements per page, and never copy the rules into a page stylesheet.

Body text is 16 px (--aha-size-l) at a 720 px measure; h2 is 32 px and h3 24 px, stepping down to 24 px and 20 px below 768 px. Use h2 for sections and h3 inside them; the article title (h1) sits outside the prose root.
Every h2 carries an id so a table of contents or a shared link can jump to it; the heading lands 96 px below the top of the window.

A callout is info, tip or warning: the tone class plus its icon (system-info, system-lightbulb-filament, system-warning-circle). The icon carries the tone; never add a status colour, border or tinted text.

Wrap every table in .aha-article-prose__table with tabindex="0", role="region" and an aria-label. It has one header row in thead and no merged cells; a wide table scrolls sideways inside its frame while the page stays put.

Inline marks are b or strong, i or em, code, s or del, and links. A link is underlined in the link colour, keeps that colour once visited, and shows the focus ring on keyboard focus; inside a quote or callout it is the text colour at rest and turns Darker Pink on hover and press (colour rule 6.5).

Cards and the FAQ are composed from DS parts, never new article classes: <aha-card> with <aha-tag> in <aha-grid>, and the Marketing FAQ section outside the prose root. Videos and charts use their own figure classes (ARTICLE-12, ARTICLE-13).
Every picture has alt text, and a caption goes in figcaption, never in a paragraph under the image.
Use .aha-article-pullquote only to repeat and highlight a sentence from the article itself, at most once between two sections; a quote from a person or a source is a plain blockquote.
A gallery is a figure.aha-article-gallery with 2 to 4 .aha-article-gallery__item figures inside .aha-article-gallery__grid, and one optional figcaption after the grid. Every picture has alt text.

Size a picture only with aha-article-figure--wide, --full or --small on a direct child figure of the prose root; wide and full bleed need the .aha-article-frame wrapper around the root. Never set a figure width or negative margin per page.

A video is a click-to-load facade: figure.aha-article-video holding .aha-article-video__frame with one <button type="button" class="aha-article-video__play" aria-label="Play video: <title>" data-provider data-video-id>, a poster img (YouTube only; else the neutral tile), the play icon and the visible title. lib/article-video.js swaps the button for the provider's iframe (youtube-nocookie.com, player.vimeo.com or loom.com/embed) on click; nothing plays or loads from the provider before the click, and nothing ever plays with sound on its own.

A chart is figure.aha-article-chart: a title, an optional unit line, one <aha-chart palette="brand"> (column, bar, line or donut), a server-rendered table in <details class="aha-article-chart__data"> under a Show data summary, and a figcaption "Source: …". The table holds the same numbers as the chart and its region is labelled "Data for <title>"; before the chart upgrades the table shows open in its place.

reuseNote: lib/article.css is the class layer (import '@ahaslides-product/design/article.css'); ARTICLE_PROSE_CSS from '@ahaslides-product/design/article-css' is the same rules as a string, for a host that injects styles (an editor iframe or shadow root).

examples.title: Headings, lists and inline marks
examples.summary: Paragraphs, an h2 with an anchor id, an h3, nested and numbered lists, bold, italic, code, a struck-through word, a link and a divider.
examples.html:
Live polls turn a talk into a conversation. This guide shows how to run one in three steps, with an optional word cloud at the end. Find every setting in the settings panel, or type /poll on a new slide.

Set up your first poll

Pick a question your audience can answer in five seconds. Short options beat long ones.

What you need

  • A free AhaSlides account
  • A question with two to five options
    • Keep each option under six words
  1. Create a new presentation.
  2. Add a Poll slide and type your question.
  3. Share the join code and present.

The old Quick vote slide is now the Poll slide.

Next, read how to show the results live.

examples.summary: A quote on Vivid Pink at 5% with its cite, and a figure whose caption sits centred under the picture.
examples.html:

examples.title: Pull quote
examples.summary: A sentence from the article set large and centred between two hairlines, with an optional attribution. A quote from someone else stays a plain blockquote.
examples.html:

examples.title: Image gallery
examples.summary: Two to four pictures with optional captions and one caption below. Three sit in three columns; below 480 px they stack.
examples.html: A gallery holds two to four pictures, each with its own caption if it needs one.

examples.title: Picture sizes
examples.summary: Small, content width, wide and full bleed. Wide and full bleed need the .aha-article-frame wrapper.
examples.html:
A small picture sits at the start of the column and the text wraps beside it. Use it for a detail that supports the paragraph, such as one button or an icon in context. Below 480 px it takes the full column.

examples.title: Callouts
examples.summary: Info and warning on the light grey fill, tip on Vivid Pink at 5%, each carried by its icon; the promo callout below them has a heading and one button.
examples.html:
Polls work on any phone browser. Your audience never installs an app.

Ask the warm-up question before your first slide, while people are still finding their seats.

Closing a poll hides it from phones straight away. Close it only after the last vote.

Try it with your next talk

Make a poll in under a minute, free.
